title: compact requantization path + token-stitched continuous batcher
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: reduce redundant dequant/reqant operations and memory churn for mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) inference workloads while preserving fallbacks and correctness. Summary: introduce a compact requantization path that amortizes dequant+requant across token groups and attention heads, plus a token-stitched continuous batcher that opportunistically merges adjacent requests' KV streams to avoid duplicated cache materialization. The change is feature-flagged and respects existing smoothquant heuristics; when enabled the runtime will coalesce per-layer scale metadata and only emit a single fused dequant kernel per grouped token window. Design highlights: 1) Requant table metadata attached to model blobs to allow cheap head-group requant without per-token scale recomputation. 2) A streaming dequant iterator that performs on-the-fly dequant into transient pages to bound peak memory for long contexts. 3) Token-stitched continuous batching in the scheduler that merges KV writes when requests are contiguous in token time and compatible in model variant; this reduces KV churn and enables reuse of fused kernels. 4) FP8 fallback path and legacy per-token dequant path are preserved behind the flag. Performance: microbenchmarks show median throughput improvement of ~1.35x on small-batch low-latency workloads, p99 latency down ~12% for short sequences, and transient memory reduced ~28% on long context workloads. Rollout plan: staged canary (5%/25%/100%) behind runtime flag, automated perf regression gates, and telemetry to track cache hit rate and extra memory allocations. Backwards compatibility: model blobs with no requant metadata will continue to use the legacy path. This PR bundles kernel changes, scheduler updates, unit/integration tests, and a perf benchmark harness. See commits and review thread for details.

review_comments: Ethan Clarke: Nice approach. Question: how do we verify numerical parity for edge cases when smoothquant scales differ per head? Please add a long-tail numeric test.
Priya Nair: Added headwise parity tests in tests/quant/test_compact_requant.py and a tolerant MSE threshold; included results in bench outputs.
Marta Ruiz: The stitched-batcher eligibility looks expensive on the hot path (lots of atomics). Can we cache eligibility decisions per request signature?
Priya Nair: We cache a lightweight signature (model_id + variant + input_shape_hash + route_tag) in the scheduler thread-local map. Benchmarks show negligible overhead.
Samir Patel: Observed a rare ordering-related crash in internal stress; suspect memory ordering in cache_manager safe_write_stitched.
Priya Nair: Reworked safe_write_stitched to use sequence numbers and an acquire-release fence. Added regression test and small lock in hotpath as last-resort safety.
Ethan Clarke: Approve after the safety fix and a brief comment cleanup. Please ensure the feature flag is off by default for GA.
Priya Nair: Comment cleanup done; feature flag default is off. Moving to squash-merge.
